title: Before the first song
blurb: Help music fans save a festival set for offline listening.

screens.heading: Help people finish a task.
screens.body: UX means user experience. Designers study what people need, then test ways to help.

screens.heading: Start rough. Learn fast.
screens.body: A wireframe is a rough screen layout. A prototype is a test version of a design.

screens.heading: Try it.
screens.question: What should guide a design change?

options.label: What people need and what tests show
options.why: Evidence helps the team choose what to improve.

options.label: Which color the designer likes best
options.why: Personal taste does not show whether a task works.

preGame.missionLine: Build your skills. Design careers can follow different paths.

ladderBranches.label: Management path
ladderBranches.roles: Design Manager → Director → VP of Design

preGame.ladderNote: Titles vary by company. These are career paths, not promised promotions.

endings.headline: A set worth saving
endings.message: You helped the team make a clearer design.
endings.subline: Level 1 complete. Later projects are not built yet.

endings.headline: Revise and retry
endings.message: Use the feedback to improve your next attempt.

endings.headline: This attempt ends here
endings.message: Take a fresh run and use what you learned.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Each scored decision adds or removes 6. Reach 85 to pass.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your first day.
beats.body: Arjun, your mentor, welcomes you to Northline’s music-app design team.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The festival is tonight.
beats.body: AMPLIFY needs fans to save a set before losing cell service. Your test could prevent a messy launch.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Samira leads the review.
beats.body: Samira leads the client demo. Your findings will shape what the team presents.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: You have a team.
beats.body: Noah builds the prototype. Amina checks access. Your research guides their next change.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Fans need music without service. What should you watch them try?

choices.label: Save a set, then open it offline.
choices.why: That task tests the actual need.

choices.label: Choose a favorite album cover.
choices.why: A cover preference does not test offline listening.

choices.label: Rate the app’s colors.
choices.why: Color ratings do not test the task.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim before checking what happened

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Start with a sketch.
beats.body: A wireframe is a rough layout. A prototype is a version people can try.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Choose two things to record during an offline-save test.
beats.whenRight: Actions and results show whether the task works.
beats.whenWrong: Record what happened during the task, not guesses or preferences.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim before checking what happened

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Eleanor misses the control.
beats.body: The fan taps the cover twice. “Where do I save this?” The Save control sits below a long description.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Save sits below a long description. Which change should you test first?

choices.label: Move Save beside the set title.
choices.why: One clear change tests whether people can find it.

choices.label: Change every label and color.
choices.why: Many changes make the result harder to explain.

choices.label: Remove offline saving.
choices.why: That removes the feature fans need.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim before checking what happened

beats.speaker: Samira
beats.title: The design lead joins.
beats.body: Samira wants your finding, not a long report.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Two fans finished the test. Flag both claims that go beyond that result.
beats.whenRight: Keep the finding as narrow as the evidence.
beats.whenWrong: Flag the claims about every fan and never failing.

rows.label: Every fan will find Save.
rows.why: Two people cannot represent every fan.

rows.label: The app never fails offline.
rows.why: This test did not cover every offline situation.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim before checking what happened

intro.line: Arjun and Samira check your work.

pass.title: A strong first pass.
pass.body: Keep going. The next task is ready.

fail.title: You can recover.
fail.body: Use the feedback on your next task.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: A new snag.
beats.body: The button is easier to find. Now Amina checks whether everyone can reach it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Tab reaches Save, but the selected control is invisible. What should the team change?

choices.label: Add a clear focus outline.
choices.why: A visible focus mark shows the selected control.

choices.label: Require everyone to use a mouse.
choices.why: Some people cannot use a mouse.

choices.label: Hide the Save button.
choices.why: Hiding it makes the task harder.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim before checking what happened

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Noah asks for help.
beats.body: “How do we check the fix before the festival team sees it?”

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Noah uses only a keyboard. How should he check the new focus outline?

choices.label: Press Tab and watch which control is selected.
choices.why: The outline should show where keyboard focus is.

choices.label: Only move the mouse over the button.
choices.why: A mouse check does not test keyboard focus.

choices.label: Ask whether the colors look stylish.
choices.why: Style alone does not show whether the control is usable.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The check is complete.
beats.body: Amina confirms the focus stays visible. Noah adds the change to the demo.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: What should you tell the client about two fans completing the task?

choices.label: Both finished. Next, test with more fans.
choices.why: State the result and the next check without overclaiming.

choices.label: The design works for every fan.
choices.why: Two tests cannot show what every fan will do.

choices.label: There is nothing left to improve.
choices.why: A useful result still needs further checks.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a claim beyond the test

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A place on the team.
beats.body: Arjun thanks you for making the work clearer for everyone.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The music is about to start.
beats.body: Your test notes are in the demo. See how your decisions held up.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Your first design project.
beats.body: See the result of your seven decisions.
beats.decidingNote: The team checks your design decisions.
